title: Finite rows and the abutment comparison
statement:
Let $\square$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, and let $\Ex_\square:g^{-1}Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ be the derived exchange transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] of functors $\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $\Phi'=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$. Let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ and $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$, and let $(D,E)$ and $(D',E')$ be the two exact couples of [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples], obtained by applying $\Phi$ and $\Phi'$ to the truncation triangles $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to$ (their spectral sequences are those of [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations], the first one with the exact functor $g^{-1}$ applied): thus $D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Phi\,\tau_{\leq q}K)$, $E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Phi(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]))$, the map $\alpha:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1}$ is induced by $\tau_{\leq q}K\to\tau_{\leq q+1}K$, likewise for $D',E',\alpha'$ with $\Phi'$, and the morphism of exact couples $(t_D,t_E)$ given there by the exchange morphisms has $t_D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q}K})$. Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$. Then:

1. Both couples satisfy the hypotheses of [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] ($D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<a$, and $E^{p,q}=0$ unless $p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$); so their spectral sequences converge to the canonical abutments $A^n=D^{0,n}$, $A'^n=D'^{0,n}$, with the finite filtrations $F^pA^n$, $F^pA'^n$ [def-sp-filtration] constructed there and $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pA^n$, $E'^{p,n-p}_\infty\cong\operatorname{gr}^pA'^n$.
2. The maps $\iota_n:A^n=\mathcal H^n(\Phi\,\tau_{\leq n}K)\to\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ and $\iota'_n:A'^n\to\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$ induced by $\tau_{\leq n}K\to K$ are isomorphisms, and they carry $F^pA^n$ onto
$$F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\mathcal H^n(\Phi\,\tau_{\leq n-p}K)\to\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)\bigr)$$
and $F^pA'^n$ onto the analogous $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$ (image filtrations [def-sp-image-filtration] induced by $\tau_{\leq n-p}K\to K$). Here $\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)=\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$, and this isomorphism carries $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ to $g^{-1}$ of the image of $\mathcal H^n(Rf_*\tau_{\leq n-p}K)\to\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$.
3. $\iota'_n\circ t_D^{0,n}=\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})\circ\iota_n$: under these identifications the map induced on the abutments by the morphism of exact couples is
$$\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K}):g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K).$$
4. $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})$ maps $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ into $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$ for every $p$, and the induced map $\operatorname{gr}^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)\to\operatorname{gr}^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$ is, under the identifications of (1) and (2), the map $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\to E'^{p,n-p}_\infty$ induced by the morphism of exact couples [lem-sp-couple-morphism].

proof.text: **Step 1 (the hypotheses of the half-plane theorem; claim 1).** For $q<a$ the complex $\tau_{\leq q}K$ has $\mathcal H^i(\tau_{\leq q}K)=\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i\leq q$ and $=0$ for $i>q$, so $\tau_{\leq q}K\cong0$ in $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ and $D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Phi(0))=0$, $D'^{p,q}=0$; likewise $\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]=0$ gives $E^{p,q}=E'^{p,q}=0$ for $q<a$. Now let $q$ be arbitrary: the complex $\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]$ has its only cohomology in degree $q$, so $\mathcal H^i=0$ for $i<q$. For $\Phi$: by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] for the left exact functor $v=f_*$ on the Grothendieck abelian category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-sp-etale-dictionary] (whose derived functor is $Rf_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]), $\mathcal H^j(Rf_*(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]))=0$ for $j<q$, and since $g^{-1}$ is induced by an exact functor [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], $\mathcal H^j(g^{-1}L)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^j(L)$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], so $E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(g^{-1}Rf_*(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]))=0$ when $p+q<q$, i.e. $p<0$. For $\Phi'$: $g'^{-1}(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])$ again has $\mathcal H^i=g'^{-1}\mathcal H^i(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])=0$ for $i<q$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] for $v=f'_*$ gives $E'^{p,q}=0$ for $p<0$. The two couples are exact couples by their construction [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples]. Hence both satisfy the hypotheses of [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] with the same $a$, which supplies, for each couple, the stabilization of every entry, the finite, exhaustive and separated filtration $F^pA^n=G_{n-p}A^n$ of $A^n=D^{0,n}$ with $G_qA^n=\operatorname{im}(\alpha^{n-q}:D^{n-q,q}\to D^{0,n})$ for $q\leq n$ and $G_qA^n=A^n$ for $q\geq n$, and $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong F^pA^{p+q}/F^{p+1}A^{p+q}$.

source.place: Lemma 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), with the blueprint proof (## Detailed form, Proof, sentences 1-4) for the vanishing of the couple terms

proof.text: **Step 2 (the abutments are the cohomology of the whole complexes; first half of claim 2).** Let $c_n:\tau_{\leq n}K\to K$ be the canonical map; $\mathcal H^i(c_n)$ is an isomorphism for $i\leq n$, and a monomorphism for $i=n+1$ because $\mathcal H^{n+1}(\tau_{\leq n}K)=0$. For $\Phi$: by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso] for $v=f_*$, $\mathcal H^n(Rf_*c_n)$ is an isomorphism; applying the exact functor $g^{-1}$ and the natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}L)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(L)$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], $\iota_n=\mathcal H^n(\Phi c_n)$ is an isomorphism. For $\Phi'$: $\mathcal H^i(g'^{-1}c_n)\cong g'^{-1}\mathcal H^i(c_n)$ naturally [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], which is an isomorphism for $i\leq n$ and, $g'^{-1}$ being exact on sheaves [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], a monomorphism for $i=n+1$; so [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso] for $v=f'_*$ applied to $g'^{-1}c_n$ shows that $\iota'_n=\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}c_n)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), part (2); the blueprint proof (## Detailed form, Proof: 'Both functors carry $\tau_{\geq n+1}K$ to complexes with no cohomology in degrees $\leq n$')

proof.text: **Step 3 (the filtrations; second half of claim 2).** For $q\leq n$ let $j_{q,n}:\tau_{\leq q}K\to\tau_{\leq n}K$ be the composite of the maps $\tau_{\leq r}K\to\tau_{\leq r+1}K$; then $\alpha^{n-q}:D^{n-q,q}\to D^{0,n}$ is $\mathcal H^n(\Phi j_{q,n})$ by functoriality of $\mathcal H^n\circ\Phi$ (definition of $\alpha$, Step 1), and $c_n\circ j_{q,n}=c_q$. Hence $\iota_n(G_qA^n)=\operatorname{im}(\mathcal H^n(\Phi c_n)\circ\mathcal H^n(\Phi j_{q,n}))=\operatorname{im}\mathcal H^n(\Phi c_q)$. For $q\geq n$, $c_n=c_q\circ j_{n,q}$ and $\mathcal H^n(\Phi c_n)$ is surjective (Step 2), so $\operatorname{im}\mathcal H^n(\Phi c_q)=\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)=\iota_n(A^n)=\iota_n(G_qA^n)$. With $F^p=G_{n-p}$ this gives $\iota_n(F^pA^n)=\operatorname{im}(\mathcal H^n(\Phi\tau_{\leq n-p}K)\to\mathcal H^n(\Phi K))$ for every $p$, i.e. $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ is the image filtration [def-sp-image-filtration] of $(A^n,F)$ along the isomorphism $\iota_n$; the same computation with $\Phi'$ and $\iota'_n$ gives the claim for $\Phi'$. Finally, the natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}L)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(L)$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] is natural in $L$, hence carries $\operatorname{im}\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*c_q)$ to $\operatorname{im}g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(Rf_*c_q)=g^{-1}\operatorname{im}\mathcal H^n(Rf_*c_q)$, an exact functor preserving images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]: this is $g^{-1}$ of the image filtration of [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] on $\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$.

**Step 4 (the abutment map is $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})$; claim 3).** By [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples], $t_D^{0,n}=\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq n}K})$. Since $\Ex_\square:\Phi\to\Phi'$ is a natural transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], its naturality square for $c_n$ reads $\Ex_{\square,K}\circ\Phi(c_n)=\Phi'(c_n)\circ\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq n}K}$; applying $\mathcal H^n$ gives $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})\circ\iota_n=\iota'_n\circ t_D^{0,n}$. As $\iota_n,\iota'_n$ are isomorphisms (Step 2), $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})=\iota'_n\circ t_D^{0,n}\circ\iota_n^{-1}$, with source $\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below].

**Step 5 (filtrations and graded pieces; claim 4).** By Step 1 both couples satisfy the hypotheses of [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence], so [lem-sp-couple-morphism] applies to the morphism $(t_D,t_E)$: $t_D^{0,n}:A^n\to A'^n$ maps $F^pA^n$ into $F^pA'^n$ for every $p$, and the induced map $\operatorname{gr}^pA^n\to\operatorname{gr}^pA'^n$ corresponds, under $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pA^n$ and $E'^{p,n-p}_\infty\cong\operatorname{gr}^pA'^n$, to the map $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\to E'^{p,n-p}_\infty$ induced by the morphism of couples. By Step 3, $\iota_n(F^pA^n)=F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ and $\iota'_n(F^pA'^n)=F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$, so $\iota_n$, $\iota'_n$ are isomorphisms of filtered objects [def-sp-filtration] and induce isomorphisms $\operatorname{gr}^p\iota_n$, $\operatorname{gr}^p\iota'_n$ of graded pieces. By Step 4, $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})=\iota'_n\circ t_D^{0,n}\circ\iota_n^{-1}$ therefore maps $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ into $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$, and its map on $\operatorname{gr}^p$ is $\operatorname{gr}^p\iota'_n\circ\operatorname{gr}^p(t_D^{0,n})\circ(\operatorname{gr}^p\iota_n)^{-1}$, which is the $E_\infty$-map under the composite identifications $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pA^n\cong\operatorname{gr}^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ and their primed versions.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
In total degree $n$, the two exact couples have only the finite row range
$a\leq q\leq n$. Their induced abutment map is the cohomology map

$$
\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)\longrightarrow
\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)
$$

of the derived exchange morphism, with the image filtrations of Definition
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations].
blueprint_sketch.proof:
On $\mathcal E_1^{p,q}$ one has $p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$. The equality
$p+q=n$ therefore forces $a\leq q\leq n$. On a hypercover total complex,
only these finitely many filtered quotients contribute to degree $n$.
Consequently direct-sum and product totalization agree in that degree, the
filtration is finite and separated, and passage from a finite skeleton to
the full hypercover changes none of its graded terms.

The maps $e_q:A_q\to B_q$ commute with
$\tau_{\leq q}K\to K$. For $q\geq n$, the omitted cohomology sheaves of
$K$ have degrees greater than $n$; after a nonnegative right-derived
functor they cannot contribute to total degree $n$. Hence

$$
\mathcal H^n(A_q)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K),\qquad
\mathcal H^n(B_q)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K).
$$

Under these identifications, $\mathcal H^n(e_q)$ is
$\mathcal H^n(\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K})$ by naturality of exchange in
the truncation map. Its filtration is the image of
$\mathcal H^n(A_q)$ and maps to the image of $\mathcal H^n(B_q)$, exactly
the two filtrations defined earlier. Thus the exact-couple abutment map is
the specified derived exchange map, rather than an unnamed filtered
isomorphism.

split_report.summary: The imported statement only named the abutment map and pointed vaguely at 'the image filtrations of [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples]'; the target thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below (Step 6) also needs that this map respects the filtrations and induces the E_infinity map on graded pieces. The statement is restated self-contained in four claims: (1) both couples satisfy the hypotheses of thm-sp-half-plane-convergence, (2) the canonical abutments D^{0,n} are identified with H^n(Phi K), H^n(Phi' K) by tau_{<=n}K -> K, carrying the half-plane filtration to the image filtration of H^n(Phi tau_{<=n-p}K) (and, for Phi, to g^{-1} of the filtration of def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations), (3) under these the abutment map t_D^{0,n} is H^n(Ex_{square,K}), (4) it respects the filtrations and induces the E_infinity map on gr (lem-sp-couple-morphism, transported). The proof follows the blueprint's 'Detailed form' proof; its first proof (hypercover total complexes, product vs sum totalization, 'finite skeleton') is unrelated to this construction and was not used. The vanishing of R^p for p<0 and the truncation comparison H^n(Rv tau_{<=n}K) = H^n(RvK) that the blueprint asserts without argument became two new nodes from Stacks 05TC. lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence is no longer cited (Step 1 checks the hypotheses of the half-plane theorem directly, including the vanishing of D for q<a which that node does not state). lem-sp-couple-morphism and thm-sp-half-plane-convergence belong to unit sk-prop-av-pqf-finite and are used as generic tool lemmas.
